key_insight: Integrating DMAIC with two-level Fuzzy AHP identified defects as the dominant waste and prioritized machine, method, and operator factors behind sidebeam bogie-frame welding defects.
engineering_relevance: The findings guide robotic welding improvement priorities toward seam tracking, robot parameters, fixture positioning, tack welding, and fit-up control.
method: DMAIC with value stream mapping, time study, u′-control chart, DPMO, and sigma analysis.
First-level Fuzzy AHP using judgments from 10 experts to rank four waste categories.
6M fishbone analysis and second-level Fuzzy AHP to prioritize potential cause categories.
evidence_signal: Across 21 inspected units, 485 defects yielded 136,658.21 DPMO and a 2.60 sigma level; undercut represented 57.1% of defects, and process cycle efficiency was 4.88%.
watch_item: Weak expert agreement and respondent-sensitive rankings limit prioritization confidence; the proposed improvements still require implementation and empirical validation.
paper_title: Integration of DMAIC and Two-Level Fuzzy AHP for Diagnosing and Prioritizing Waste and Potential Causes of Welding Defects in a Sidebeam Bogie Frame
